mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Velar D240 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Range Rover Velar D240 engine typically costs between £5,200 and £7,500 for supply only. Reconditioned units start around £3,500, while used engines can be found from £2,000. Prices vary based on whether you choose supply-only or a full supply and fit service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain or turbo failure in a Range Rover Velar D240?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include a distinct metallic rattling noise from the engine bay during cold starts, which may fade as the oil warms up. You might also experience loss of power, excessive smoke, or an illuminated check engine light due to timing stretch or turbo bearing failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Velar D240?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the current premium vehicle market. A well-maintained Range Rover Velar D240 holds a value of £15,000 to £35,000+. Investing £5,200-£7,500 in a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is financially viable and protects the appreciating asset value of this premium SUV.

mainEntity.name: What is the 204DTA engine code in the Range Rover Velar D240?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 204DTA (also known as AJ20D4) is the specific 2.0-litre four-cylinder twin-turbo Ingenium diesel engine code fitted to the Range Rover Velar D240 (producing 240PS). It features advanced common-rail injection and, in later model years, a mild-hybrid electrical system (MHEV) for improved efficiency.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Velar D240 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Range Rover Velar D240 typically takes 2 to 3 working days. This includes the removal of the old unit, thorough cleaning of the engine bay, installation of the replacement engine, and comprehensive software calibration.

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Oil Dilution - Why the Range Rover Velar D240 204DTA Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Incomplete DPF regeneration cycles dump diesel fuel past piston rings into the engine oil. Rising oil level reduces viscosity until bearings fail. Additionally, the twin-turbo arrangement subjects the high-pressure turbo to extreme thermal cycling, and early timing chain tensioners can wear, leading to chain stretch.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Oil and filter change with correct STJLR.03.5006 spec, forced DPF regen, timing chain inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage symptoms without metallic rattling or chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit reconditioned long engine with upgraded timing components and revised piston rings, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for catastrophic chain failure, turbo metal contamination, or severe oil dilution damage
